Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt to your own workflow).  
I’ll also show the exact Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions workflow that you can drop into the repo.  

> ⚠️ **Important** – I can’t actually run `git clone` or `git push` from here, but the commands below will do it for you locally.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & generate artefacts

### 2.1 Dockerfile

> *Assumption:* The repo contains a standard Node.js app that listens on port **3000** (`server.js` or similar).

```bash
cat <<'EOF' > Dockerfile
# Use a lightweight Node.js runtime
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set maintainer
LABEL maintainer="Your Name <you@example.com>"

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package.json + lockfile first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the listening port
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
EOF
```

> If the app uses a different entry point (e.g., `app.js`, `index.js`) adjust the `CMD` accordingly.

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

> *Assumption:* You want a **LoadBalancer** service exposing port 3000, with 2 replicas.

```bash
cat <<'EOF' > k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change to your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # Service port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
EOF
```

> *Tip:* If you’re using Docker Hub, replace the image URL with `dockerhub_user/nodejs-welcome:latest`.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml`:

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cat <<'EOF' > .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Cache Docker layers
        uses: actions/cache@v3
        with:
          path: /tmp/.buildx-cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
EOF
```

> **What this does**  
> • Builds the image on every push to `main`.  
> • Pushes it to GitHub Container Registry under `ghcr.io/<owner>/nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> • Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication (no extra secrets needed).

---

## 3️⃣ Add, Commit & Push

```bash
# Stage all new/changed files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml

# Commit with a meaningful message
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to remote
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically trigger and build/push the Docker image.

---

## 4️⃣ Verify

1. **GitHub Actions** – Go to *Actions* tab → see the “Build & Push Docker Image” job succeed.  
2. **Docker image** – Check GHCR: `ghcr.io/<owner>/nodejs-welcome:latest` (or Docker Hub if you changed the registry).  
3. **Kubernetes** – Deploy the manifest to your cluster:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Check the service IP:

```bash
kubectl get svc nodejs-welcome
```

If you’re on a cloud provider, the external IP will appear once the LoadBalancer is provisioned.

---

### Recap of Files Added

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deployment + LoadBalancer service |
| `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image |

Feel free to tweak the image tags, registry, or Kubernetes settings to fit your environment. Happy coding!
